# ADR-0001 — Stack and defaults ({{date}})

Status: accepted · supersedes: — · superseded by: —

In the context of starting {{product}} with GYOS, facing the need for boundaries that hold from the
first commit, we decided for a modular monolith on GYOS's defaults (and against microservices or a
hand-picked stack), to achieve one deployable with enforced module boundaries, accepting the
defaults until there is a reason to change one.

## Context

{{product}} is built by {{a solo engineer / a small team}}. Network boundaries between services
would cost more than they give at this size; boundaries that hold inside one codebase are what
matters. The defaults are the ones GYOS verifies end to end.

## Decision

| | Choice |
| --- | --- |
| Shape | Modular monolith: one host app, one module per bounded context ([docs/standards/module.md](../standards/module.md)) |
| Runtime | Node {{node-version}} |
| Workspace | pnpm workspaces + Turborepo |
| Language | TypeScript, strict, ESM, erasable syntax only |
| Host app | Express ([apps/api](../../apps/api/)) |
| Frontend | {{React / Svelte / Vue}}, {{scaffolder and meta-framework}}, because {{SSR or SEO needed or not}} |
| Database | Postgres, one schema per module |
| ORM | Drizzle |
| Validation | Zod at every boundary |
| Module build | `tsc`, with the `@gyos/source` condition for development |
| Boundaries | Architecture tests in Vitest |

{{Any default the user changed, with the reason; or "None changed."}}

## Options considered

- **Microservices:** independent deploys and scaling, at the cost of network calls, distributed
  data and several pipelines, with no team-size reason to pay it.
- **A hand-picked stack:** possible, but every default above is verified together by GYOS; a
  change is made by superseding this ADR.

## Consequences

- Moving a boundary is a refactoring inside one repo, not a migration between services.
- A module can still be extracted later, because it owns its schema and talks through its entry
  points.
- Changing a default means a new ADR that supersedes this one.

Confirmation: invariant: M7; invariant: M10
Confidence: high. Revisit when: one module needs independent scaling or a different deploy cadence.
